title: CI / Cloudflare Access service-token readiness
purpose: Keep automated CI authentication through Cloudflare Access separate from authenticated browser acceptance and expose the exact safe correction mechanics without inspecting, storing or revealing secret values.

authority_separation.browser_runtime: Release 467 Build 3 and Build 4 browser evidence proves same-origin authenticated admin runtime only.
authority_separation.ci_access: A browser PASS is never CI Access proof. CI Access remains HOLD_EXTERNAL until an independent Development workflow succeeds using the approved Cloudflare Access service token.
authority_separation.application_admin: A Cloudflare Access service token is not application-admin authentication and must not be treated as an admin session.
authority_separation.production: No Build 5 evidence authorizes Production access or mutation.

manual_correction_mechanics: Create or reuse a Cloudflare Access service token accepted by the Development host only.
Store the client ID as the GitHub Actions repository secret CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_ID.
Store the client secret as the GitHub Actions repository secret CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_SECRET.
Use the token only in a bounded Development CI acceptance workflow that sends CF-Access-Client-Id and CF-Access-Client-Secret headers.
Do not echo, serialize, download or persist either secret value.
Do not infer application-admin authentication from successful Cloudflare Access authentication.
Capture only sanitized workflow evidence after the Development check succeeds.

closure_condition: CI Access may move from HOLD_EXTERNAL only after an independently observed Development-only workflow succeeds with the Cloudflare Access service token and sanitized evidence is captured. That success does not prove application-admin authentication and does not authorize Production.
blocked_mutations: Development D1 or R2 business-data mutation
Cloudflare Access policy or token creation from the application
GitHub repository secret creation from the application
